messages.subject: Feedback - Mittens
messages.text:
My husband and I each ordered a pair of mittens. We are using them when we go downhill skiing and they are definitely keeping our hands and fingers warm. We bought a medium and a large pair — they are the right sizes for us but we both have found that the mittens
 are a bit too long — about ¾ inch too long. 

 

 
Adding a loop to the mittens would also be a very simple but good idea. When I'm bundled up, come into the ski lodge for quick break to use the toilet, I can't hang my mittens up where they will be safe and stay dry. 

 

 
I don't know how Common Milkweed is viewed in other provinces, but in Nova Scotia, where we currently live, Common Milkweed is actually considered a noxious week, primarily because it can interfere with agricultural crops. Rather than planting Common Milkweed,
 Nova Scotians are encouraged to plant Swamp Milkweed which is a native plant in this part of Canada. When selling the seeds, it would be helpful to let buyers know which seeds are best suited to their area. 

 

 
Keep up the great, innovative and important work.

 

 
Susan

messages.subject: Re: Feedback - Mittens
messages.text:
Hi Susan,

Thank you for taking the time to share all this, really useful feedback on every point.

The length issue is noted. We'll flag it to our product team as something to look at for the next iteration. The loop idea is also genuinely good: simple, practical, and the kind of thing that makes a real difference on a ski day.

On the milkweed side, you're absolutely right that Common Milkweed (Asclepias syriaca) is classified as a noxious weed in Nova Scotia, and Swamp Milkweed (Asclepias incarnata) is the better native option for the Maritimes. We do sell Incarnata seeds and seed bombs, and your point about making regional guidance more visible on our product pages is well taken. We'll bring it up.

Glad the mittens are keeping you both warm on the slopes!

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
